diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with gray-white centers and brown margins on leaves; severe black necrotic constriction at panicle neck node leading to complete grain chaffiness (neck blast).

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Intermittent drizzle / cloudy weather creating prolonged leaf wetness

management.cultural_controls: Balanced fertilizer application (split N into 3 doses, avoid >100 kg N/ha); maintain 5 cm water level during blast-favorable cold dew periods; burn infected stubbles.
management.biological_controls: Rhizosphere application of Trichoderma harzianum; foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (2x10^9 CFU/mL).
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Tricyclazole 75 WP (Trooper / Beam @ 0.75 g/L); Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (Amistar Top @ 1 mL/L); Kasugamycin 2% (Kasu-B @ 2 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Apply first spray at late booting stage; second spray 7-10 days later at 50% ear emergence. Ensure uniform panicle coverage.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BRRI dhan89, BRRI dhan92, BRRI dhan65, BRRI dhan58
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant to Resistant (Field tolerance to leaf and neck blast)
resistant_varieties.known_susceptible_varieties: BRRI dhan28, BRRI dhan29 (highly susceptible, obsolete)

seasonal_calendar.risk_months: February, March, April (Boro); September, October (T. Aman)
seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Seedling (leaf blast), Booting to Heading (neck and node blast)
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Every 2-3 days during heading stage when morning dew exceeds 8 hours
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Apply prophylactic Tricyclazole 75 WP at late booting and 7 days later at 50% heading.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy, yellowish-white necrotic bands; bacterial ooze droplets on leaves during high morning humidity; 'kresek' systemic seedling wilt.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Heavy monsoon showers with gusty winds causing mechanical leaf abrasion
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp >= 26C) AND (RH >= 85%) AND (windy storm rainfall event occurred)

management.cultural_controls: Drain water from infected fields for 3-4 days; delay nitrogen top-dressing; apply 5 kg/bigha muriate of potash (MOP); avoid clipping seedling tips at transplanting.
management.biological_controls: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis strain BRRI-BS1; seed bacterization with Pseudomonas putida.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Copper hydroxide 77 WP (Champion @ 2 g/L); Bismerthiazol 20 WP (Bactroban @ 1.5 g/L); Validamycin 3L (@ 2 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray early morning upon detection of water-soaked stripes; repeat after 7 days if weather remains rainy.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BRRI dhan31, BRRI dhan48, BRRI dhan81
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant (Carries Xa4 and Xa21 introgressions)

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly; inspect immediately after cyclonic rain/wind storm events
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Drain excess standing water, top-dress 5 kg/bigha potash, avoid excessive nitrogen urea.

diseases.symptoms: Oval, water-soaked greenish-gray spots with dark brown margins developing on leaf sheaths near water line; lesions coalesce forming extensive snake-skin patterns ascending to upper leaves.

climate_rules.soil_moisture_trigger: Standing floodwater / prolonged water depth > 5 cm
climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: High seasonal rainfall with warm stagnant field water
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 28-32C) AND (microclimate_RH >= 90%) AND (dense canopy closed)

management.cultural_controls: Wider hill spacing (20x20 cm); remove floating organic skimmings and sclerotia during final land puddling; avoid excessive tillering via controlled N.
management.biological_controls: Trichoderma harzianum fermented compost application (100 kg/ha); antagonistic Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Thifluzamide 24 SC (Pulsor @ 0.5 mL/L); Hexaconazole 5 EC (Contaf @ 1 mL/L); Validamycin 3% L (Sheathmar @ 2 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Direct spray towards basal leaf sheaths and stem bases near water surface; 2 sprays at 10-day intervals.

resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Tolerant (Erect canopy architecture escapes humidity)

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Active tillering to milk stage (dense canopy closure)
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Twice weekly; inspect basal leaf sheaths near water line
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Maintain spacing (20x15 cm), avoid dense clumps, apply Thifluzamide 24 SC at first lesion sight.

diseases.symptoms: Premature bleaching of individual spikelets or entire wheat heads while leaves remain green; blackened rachis node infection causing shriveled, chaffy, unfillable grains.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Pre-monsoon / late winter light rains or unseasonal rains during heading stage
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: CRITICAL if (growth_stage == 'heading') AND (temp between 22-28C) AND (RH >= 85% for 48h consecutive)

management.cultural_controls: Plant resistant cultivars (BARI Gom 33, WMRI Gom 3); sow wheat between Nov 15 - Nov 30 to escape February warm rains during heading; collect and destroy infected straw.
management.biological_controls: Garlic bulb extract (allicin-rich, 1:10 w/v); Streptomyces oligomycins formulations.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Tebuconazole 50% + Trifloxystrobin 25% WG (Nativo 75 WG @ 0.6 g/L); Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (Amistar Top @ 1 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Preventative spray at complete head emergence (Gom-ber-hobar somoy); if rainy weather persists, repeat spray 7 days later.

resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Resistant (Carries 2NS chromosome translocation from Aegilops ventricosa; biofortified with 51 ppm Zinc)
resistant_varieties.known_susceptible_varieties: Prodip, BARI Gom 26, Shatabdi (discontinued in blast-prone zones)

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Daily from ear emergence to anthesis (critical 14-day window)
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Plant blast-resistant BARI Gom 33; if susceptible variety grown, spray Nativo 75 WG (0.6 g/L) at heading.

diseases.symptoms: Small, chlorotic specks expanding into elliptical brown necrotic blotches (1-2 cm) with bright yellow halos; progressive foliar blighting causing premature canopy desiccation.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Warm rainfall followed by sunny intervals
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp >= 24C) AND (RH >= 80%) AND (post-anthesis terminal heat stress present)

management.cultural_controls: Seed treatment with certified fungicides; practice 2-year crop rotation with non-host legumes; optimal irrigation to avoid terminal drought stress.
management.biological_controls: Seed priming with Trichoderma harzianum; Pseudomonas fluorescens liquid formulation.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% WS (Provax-200 @ 2.5 g/kg seed); Propiconazole 25 EC (Tilt 250 EC @ 0.5 mL/L); Tebuconazole 250 EC (Folicur @ 0.5 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Seed treatment prior to sowing; foliar spray at boot stage and milk stage if flag leaf displays >5% necrotic blotches.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Gom 28, BARI Gom 30, BARI Gom 31
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant (Superior membrane stability under terminal heat stress)

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Tillering, flag leaf emergence, grain filling
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly scouting of lower leaves for brown pinpoint blotches
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Seed treatment with Provax-200 (Carboxin + Thiram @ 2.5 g/kg seed); avoid late sowing past Dec 5.

diseases.disease_name: Maydis Leaf Blight / Southern Corn Leaf Blight
diseases.symptoms: Small diamond-shaped or elongated rectangular lesions bounded by leaf veins; buff to tan centers with reddish-brown borders coalescing into extensive foliar blighting.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Frequent light rainfall and humid overcast periods

management.cultural_controls: Deep autumn plowing to bury crop debris; balanced NPK with adequate potassium (60 kg K2O/ha); crop rotation with pulses or potato.
management.biological_controls: Trichoderma viride seed treatment (10 g/kg seed); foliar bio-fungicide formulations.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Mancozeb 75 WP (Dithane M-45 @ 2.5 g/L); Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (Amistar Top @ 1 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray when bottom leaves show initial lesions at knee-high stage; repeat 10-14 days later.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Hybrid Maize-9, BARI Hybrid Maize-7, BARI Hybrid Maize-16
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Resistant to Moderately Resistant (Thick leaf cuticles, high yield)

seasonal_calendar.risk_months: March, April, May (Rabi maturity); June, July (Kharif-1)
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Plant resistant BARI hybrid maize; spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at first lesion onset.

diseases.symptoms: Concentric characteristic bleaching bands alternating with brownish margins on lower leaf sheaths; spreads upward to ears causing husk decay and grain molding.

climate_rules.soil_moisture_trigger: High soil surface dampness under thick canopy
climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Moderate to heavy rain keeping basal leaf sheaths saturated
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 28-32C) AND (RH >= 85%) AND (basal sheath microclimate saturated)

management.cultural_controls: Strip bottom 2-3 senescent leaf sheaths from maize stalks at 45-50 DAS to reduce humidity; maintain plant-to-plant spacing of 25 cm.
management.biological_controls: Trichoderma asperellum soil drenching around basal root crown.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Validamycin 3L (Sheathmar @ 2 mL/L); Hexaconazole 5 EC (Contaf @ 1 mL/L); Carbendazim 50 WP (Bavistin @ 1.5 g/L).
management.application_guidelines: Direct spray specifically onto lower stalk nodes and ear husks.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Hybrid Maize-14, BARI Hybrid Maize-15

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Knee-high (V8) to silking and ear development
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly; strip bottom 2 senescent leaf sheaths to eliminate microclimate
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Remove lower infected leaf sheaths; spray Validamycin 3L or Hexaconazole 5 EC at stem base.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish-brown lesions on leaves and stems surrounded by pale yellowish rings; delicate white powdery mildew-like sporangial down on leaf undersides in morning dew; brown granular dry rot inside tubers.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Dense winter fog / cold drizzle / overcast skies for > 3 consecutive days
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: CRITICAL if (night_temp between 10-15C) AND (day_temp between 18-22C) AND (RH >= 90%) AND (fog_dew_duration >= 8h)

management.cultural_controls: Use certified disease-free seed tubers; plant with wide ridge spacing (60x25 cm); ensure thorough earthing-up (hilling) to cover tubers with >=10 cm soil preventing spore wash down.
management.biological_controls: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens soil and foliar preventative applications.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Preventative: Mancozeb 75 WP (Indofil M-45 @ 2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (Daconil @ 2 g/L); Curative/Systemic: Dimethomorph 9% + Mancozeb 60% WG (Acrobat MZ @ 2 g/L) or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Curzate M8 @ 2 g/L) or Fenamidone 10% + Mancozeb 50% WG (Secure @ 1.5 g/L).
management.application_guidelines: Commence preventative sprays when weather forecast predicts dense fog / cold dew; rotate systemic chemistries every 7 days; stop irrigation.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Alu-25, BARI Alu-46, BARI Alu-53
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant (Field tolerance to Phytophthora infestans A1/A2 lineages)

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Canopy closure, tuber initiation, tuber bulking
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Daily during overcast, foggy, or dewy cold spells (<15C night temp)
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Preventative spray of Mancozeb 75 WP (2 g/L) before canopy closes; curative spray of Dimethomorph + Mancozeb upon first spot.

diseases.symptoms: Rapid daytime wilting of foliage without initial yellowing; plant may temporarily recover overnight before permanent wilt; brown discoloration of vascular ring in cut tubers; dirty white bacterial slime streaming from tuber vascular ring.

climate_rules.soil_moisture_trigger: High soil moisture / Saturated soil / Poor drainage / Waterlogging
climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Heavy monsoon rains or excessive furrow irrigation causing soil saturation
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: CRITICAL if (soil_temp >= 28.0C) AND (soil_moisture == 'saturated/waterlogged') AND (soil_pH between 6.0-7.2). Note: leaf_wetness is completely excluded.

management.cultural_controls: Plant ONLY tested, certified pathogen-free seed tubers; avoid planting whole tubers or cut seed in soils >28C; construct high beds with excellent furrow drainage; 3-year crop rotation with maize/mustard (never solanaceous crops).
management.biological_controls: Soil amendment with mustard oilcake (350 kg/ha); biological seed tuber coating with Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Bleaching powder / Calcium hypochlorite (soil treatment @ 15-20 kg/ha before planting); Copper oxychloride 50 WP (soil drench @ 3 g/L around stem base). Note: Chemical foliar sprays are INEFFECTIVE against vascular Ralstonia.
management.application_guidelines: Pre-plant furrow soil treatment with calcium hypochlorite; rogue out wilted plants with surrounding root soil and burn; sterilize harvesting knives in 5% formalin.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Alu-8, BARI Alu-40 (Field tolerant); Certified seed of BARI Alu-7
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Tolerant (Note: Complete immunity does not exist in commercial Solanum tuberosum)
resistant_varieties.known_susceptible_varieties: Cardinal, Lady Rosetta, Asterix (highly susceptible in infested soils)

seasonal_calendar.risk_months: October, November (early sowing); February, March (warming soils)
seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Early vegetative emergence and pre-harvest tuber maturation
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Twice weekly; inspect plants during midday heat for transient wilting
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Use certified pathogen-free seed tubers; avoid planting in soil temp >28C; construct high ridges to prevent waterlogging.

diseases.scientific_name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus / Geminiviridae)
diseases.symptoms: Severe upward and inward cupping and curling of leaf margins; intense interveinal chlorosis and yellowing; marked reduction in leaflet size; bushy erect stunting; severe flower drop and failure to set fruit.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Prolonged dry spells with absence of heavy rainfall (rain washes away whiteflies)
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 28-35C) AND (RH between 50-70%) AND (dry_days >= 7) AND (whitefly_vector_active)

management.cultural_controls: Raise nursery seedlings under 50-mesh nylon insect nets; install yellow sticky cards (30-40 per acre); use silver reflective plastic mulch to repel whitefly vectors; rogue out and bury early stunted plants.
management.biological_controls: Beauveria bassiana or Verticillium lecanii entomopathogenic fungi (2 g/L) to control nymphal whitefly populations.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Vector Management: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (Admire @ 0.5 mL/L) or Acetamiprid 20 SP (Tundra @ 0.5 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (Oberon @ 1 mL/L) for whitefly nymph control.
management.application_guidelines: Seedling root dip in Imidacloprid (0.5 mL/L) for 30 minutes before transplanting; alternate insecticide modes of action every 10 days to prevent whitefly resistance.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Tomato-14, BARI Tomato-15, BINA Tomato-10
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Resistant to Moderately Resistant (Carries Ty-1/Ty-3 resistance genes)

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Nursery seedling stage to early vegetative branching
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Daily yellow sticky trap monitoring in seedling nursery and transplant field
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Raise nursery under 50-mesh insect-proof netting; treat seedlings with Imidacloprid (0.5 mL/L); silver reflective mulch.

diseases.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with concentric target-board ridges on older lower leaves surrounded by chlorotic yellow halo; dark sunken collar rot on stems; dark leathery rot at fruit calyx end.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Heavy dew or frequent showers alternating with sunny periods

management.cultural_controls: Stake plants upright; prune bottom suckers and lower foliage touching soil; practice drip irrigation instead of furrow/overhead splashing; destroy tomato vine residue after harvest.
management.biological_controls: Trichoderma harzianum foliar spray (5 g/L); garlic bulb extract (1:10 w/v).
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Mancozeb 75 WP (Dithane M-45 @ 2.5 g/L); Difenoconazole 250 EC (Score @ 0.5 mL/L); Azoxystrobin 23 SC (Amistar @ 1 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray lower foliage upon first appearance of target spots; re-apply every 10 days during fruit sizing.

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Flowering, fruit set, and fruit ripening
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly; inspect lower foliage for concentric target-board lesions
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Prune bottom leaves touching soil; preventative Mancozeb spray; switch to Difenoconazole if lesions expand.

diseases.symptoms: Circular brownish-black target spots on lower leaves with concentric rings; elongated sunken black streaks on stems and siliquae (pods); pod infection results in shriveled seeds and premature shattering.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Morning winter dew / drizzle during flowering and pod development stages
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 18-24C) AND (RH >= 85%) AND (dew_duration >= 7h during flowering)

management.cultural_controls: Early sowing (October 20-30); clean cultivation; destruction of wild cruciferous weeds (Sinapis arvensis); balanced potassium application.
management.biological_controls: Seed coating with Trichoderma viride powder (10 g/kg seed).
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L); Mancozeb 75 WP (Indofil @ 2.5 g/L); Difenoconazole 25 EC (Score @ 0.5 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: First spray at 40-45 DAS (early flowering); second spray at 55-60 DAS (siliqua formation).

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Sarisha-14, BARI Sarisha-15, BARI Sarisha-17, BINA Sarisha-9
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Tolerant (Short duration 75-80 days escaping late dew peaks)

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly; examine lower leaves and developing pods
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Early sowing by late October to escape heavy January dew; spray Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L) at 45 and 60 DAS.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on lower stems covered by fluffy white cottony mycelium; stem bleaching, shredding, and premature lodging; hard black rat-dropping like sclerotia inside hollowed pith.

climate_rules.soil_moisture_trigger: Moist soil surface facilitating carpogenic sclerotial germination
climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Winter rain or post-irrigation humidity during January canopy closure
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (soil_temp between 15-20C) AND (soil_moist) AND (canopy_RH >= 85% at flowering)

management.cultural_controls: Crop rotation with non-host cereals (wheat/maize) for 2-3 seasons; deep summer plowing to bury sclerotia >10 cm; avoid excessive irrigation during flowering.
management.biological_controls: Soil incorporation of Coniothyrium minitans or Trichoderma harzianum at land preparation.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Carbendazim 50 WP (Bavistin @ 1.5 g/L); Thiophanate-methyl 70 WP (Topsin-M @ 1.5 g/L); Boscalid 50 WG (@ 1 g/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray stem base and lower canopy at 50% flowering before petals drop into leaf axils.

resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant (More resistant than B. campestris types)

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly during flowering; examine stem bases for white cottony mold
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Crop rotation with non-host cereals (wheat/maize); avoid excessive irrigation during flowering; apply Carbendazim 50 WP.

diseases.symptoms: Small pin-head sized brown specks on leaflets expanding into extensive light-brown or ash-colored blighting; rapid defoliation leaving bare twigs; complete drying up of canopy during flowering.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Dense morning fog and cloudy overcast days in late January to mid-February

management.cultural_controls: Avoid excessive seed rates; maintain optimal plant density to ensure canopy air circulation; destroy infected lentil straw post-harvest.
management.biological_controls: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum bio-fungicide (5 g/kg seed).
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L); Fenamidone 10% + Mancozeb 50% WG (Secure 600 WG @ 1.5 g/L); Difenoconazole 250 EC (Score @ 0.5 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Apply first spray immediately upon detection of leaflet blighting in late January; repeat 10 days later.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Masur-7, BARI Masur-8, BINA Masur-10
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant to Resistant against Stemphylium botryosum

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Every 3-4 days in February when morning fog persists past 9:00 AM
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Spray Rovral 50 WP (Iprodione @ 2 g/L) or Secure 600 WG (Fenamidone + Mancozeb) at first sign of leaflet discoloration.

diseases.scientific_name: Uromyces viciae-fabae / Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lentis
diseases.symptoms: Rust: Yellowish-brown pustules (uredinia) on leaves and pods turning dark brown-black (telia); Wilt: sudden drooping and wilting of plant tops, internal vascular browning of taproot.

climate_rules.soil_moisture_trigger: Wilt favored by early dry soil followed by irrigation; Rust favored by humid foliage
climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Warm rain followed by rapid temperature rise in late Rabi season
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 20-26C) AND (RH >= 75%) AND (crop at reproductive phase)

management.cultural_controls: Sow rust-resistant BARI Masur-6, 8; avoid waterlogged heavy soils; practice 2-year crop rotation.
management.biological_controls: Seed bacterization with Rhizobium leguminosarum combined with Trichoderma harzianum.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Propiconazole 25 EC (Tilt 250 EC @ 0.5 mL/L); Hexaconazole 5 EC (Contaf @ 1 mL/L); Carboxin + Thiram (Provax-200 @ 2.5 g/kg seed).
management.application_guidelines: Seed treatment for wilt; foliar spray at onset of rust pustules in February.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Masur-5, BARI Masur-6, BARI Masur-8
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Resistant to Rust (Uromyces viciae-fabae) and Fusarium wilt

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly scouting of lower leaves for brown pustules
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Sow resistant cultivars BARI Masur-6, 8; treat seeds with Trichoderma viride or Provax-200.

diseases.symptoms: Sunken circular or oblong necrotic lesions on ripe or developing fruit with concentric rings of dark acervuli releasing pinkish gelatinous spore masses; dieback of twigs from top downwards.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Rain splashes during fruit ripening phase dispersing gelatinous conidia
climate_rules.risk_model_logic: HIGH if (temp between 26-30C) AND (RH >= 80%) AND (rain_events > 0 during fruiting)

management.cultural_controls: Select disease-free ripe seed; remove and burn infected mummified fruits and twigs; avoid overhead irrigation; improve furrow drainage.
management.biological_controls: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride (10 g/kg); foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis.
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (Amistar Top @ 1 mL/L); Copper oxychloride 50 WP (Cupravit @ 3 g/L); Carbendazim 50 WP (Bavistin @ 1 g/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray during flowering and repeated twice at fruit setting during rainy intervals.

resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant to Colletotrichum fruit rot

seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Twice weekly during monsoon showers; inspect ripening fruits
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (Amistar Top @ 1 mL/L) or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L); pick diseased fruits immediately.

diseases.symptoms: Small water-soaked sunken lesions on leaves and seed scapes rapidly turning brown, then developing distinctive purple to dark purple centers surrounded by broad chlorotic yellow zones; leaf girdling and toppling.

climate_rules.rainfall_trigger: Heavy dew / unseasonal rain events in February-March

management.cultural_controls: Plant certified disease-free sets/bulbs; ensure wide row spacing; avoid nitrogen over-fertilization; destroy infected onion debris.
management.biological_controls: Bulb treatment and foliar spray with Trichoderma harzianum; spray of raw garlic extract (5%).
management.chemical_active_ingredients: Mancozeb 75 WP (Dithane M-45 @ 2.5 g/L); Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L); Propiconazole 25 EC (Tilt @ 0.5 mL/L).
management.application_guidelines: Spray at 10-14 day intervals starting when purple flecks appear on leaves or seed scapes.

resistant_varieties.variety_name: BARI Piaj-1, BARI Piaj-4, BARI Piaj-6
resistant_varieties.resistance_level: Moderately Resistant (Thick waxy leaves reduce spore adherence)

seasonal_calendar.vulnerable_growth_stages: Bulb enlargement and seed scape emergence
seasonal_calendar.monitoring_frequency: Weekly; inspect flower scapes and leaf tips
seasonal_calendar.preventative_actions: Spray Dithane M-45 (Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L) combined with garlic clove extract; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

research_papers.title: Diversity of pathogenicity among rice blast fungus (Pyricularia oryzae) isolates in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Kabir, M. S.; Mian, M. S.; Akter, S.; Latif, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Identified 18 distinct pathotypes among 75 Pyricularia oryzae isolates collected across Bangladesh. Documented high virulence on widely grown mega-varieties BRRI dhan28 and BRRI dhan29 during Boro season.

research_papers.title: Cross Infection between Rice and Wheat Blast Pathogen Pyricularia oryzae in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.; Rahman, M. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Demonstrated that Magnaporthe oryzae isolates from infected wheat heads can cause mild lesions on vulnerable rice seedlings under humid greenhouse conditions, though host specialization between MoT and MoO lineages is maintained.

research_papers.title: Management of Rice Blast (Magnaporthe Oryzae B. Couch) Using Bioagents and Fungicides in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Sultana, R.; Mia, M. A. T.; Latif, M. A.; Islam, M. R.
research_papers.key_findings: Evaluated Trichoderma harzianum and commercial fungicides; Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.75 g/L and Kasugamycin at 2 mL/L provided 82% and 76% blast suppression respectively under field conditions.

research_papers.title: Antifungal potential of commercial silver nanoparticles against rice blast pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Akter, N.; Islam, M. T.; Rahman, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Demonstrated that silver nanoparticles (30-50 nm) at 50 ppm achieved complete inhibition of conidial germination and appressorium formation in P. oryzae.

research_papers.title: Strategy for Rice Disease Management in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Kabir, M. S.
research_papers.key_findings: Comprehensive disease survey across 30 AEZs: blast and sheath blight represent 65% of all chemical fungicide interventions; highlights critical early warning need based on canopy humidity >90% and night temperatures 20-24°C.

research_papers.disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
research_papers.title: Genetic Divergence of Rice Genotypes Revealed by Bacterial Blight Disease and SSR Markers in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Akter, S.; Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Islam, M. R.
research_papers.key_findings: Screened 45 rice germplasm lines against Xoo isolates; identified functional resistance alleles Xa4 and Xa21; recommended marker-assisted introgressions into modern Boro varieties.

research_papers.disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
research_papers.title: Molecular marker assisted gene stacking for multiple diseases resistance in rice in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hasan, M. M.; Rafii, M. Y.; Latif, M. A.; Rahim, H. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Pyramided Xa21 and xa13 bacterial blight resistance genes with blast resistance genes Pi2/Pi9, achieving broad-spectrum resistance against virulent Bangladeshi strains.

research_papers.disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
research_papers.title: Identification of Rice Germplasm with Resistance to Bacterial Leaf Blight in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Latif, M. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Mia, M. A. T.
research_papers.key_findings: Screened 120 Bangladeshi and IRRI rice lines against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae; identified high resistance in BRRI dhan31 and DV85 carrying Xa5 and Xa7 genes.

research_papers.title: Biological Control of Rice Sheath Blight Disease (Rhizoctonia solani) Using Antagonistic Bacteria in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Mitu, S. A.; Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Akter, S.
research_papers.key_findings: Isolated indigenous Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens strains from rice rhizosphere; achieved 68.4% reduction in sheath blight lesion height and sustained grain weight under field microplot trials.

research_papers.title: Standardization of inoculation techniques for sheath blight of rice in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. R.
research_papers.key_findings: Established that micro-chamber Typha-strip inoculation at maximum tillering under relative humidity >90% yields uniform sheath blight infection for resistance screening.

research_papers.title: Epidemiology and management of false smut of rice (Ustilaginoidea virens) in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Latif, M. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Mia, M. A. T.
research_papers.key_findings: Documented rising incidence of false smut in hybrid and high-yielding Boro varieties receiving excessive nitrogenous fertilizers (>120 kg N/ha); yield losses reach 15-25% via smut ball formation.

research_papers.title: Historical Milestones and Genomic Evolution in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae Research
research_papers.authors: Midha, S.; Patil, P. B.; Swings, J.
research_papers.key_findings: Traces pathotype evolution of Xoo in tropical rice systems; TAL effector diversity drives susceptibility in traditional landraces.

research_papers.title: Transmission biology and vector dynamics of Rice Tungro Bacilliform and Spherical Viruses in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Kabir, M. S.; Latif, M. A.; Ali, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Nephotettix virescens green leafhopper populations surge following late monsoon rains; synchronized planting and light traps reduce vector numbers and tungro stunting incidence by over 70%.

research_papers.title: Screening of Rice Genotypes for Resistance to Blast (Pyricularia oryzae) under Subtropical Climates
research_papers.authors: Akter, S.; Mian, M. S.; Latif, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Field screening identified differential blast reaction between seedling leaf blast and reproductive neck blast; validated resistant alleles in BRRI dhan65.

research_papers.title: Morphological and Molecular Characterization of Pyricularia oryzae Isolates Causing Rice Blast
research_papers.authors: Wahyudi, T.; Prasetyo, J.; Maryono, T.
research_papers.key_findings: Demonstrates sporulation optima between 24-26°C with 100% relative humidity; appressoria melanization inhibited by tricyclazole.

research_papers.title: Head Rice Recovery, Comparative Advantage, and Disease Loss Dynamics in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Kabir, M. S.; Rahman, M. C.; Salam, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Quantified post-harvest milling losses attributed to fungal panicle glume discoloration and neck blast; grain breakage rises by 35% in blast-affected lots.

research_papers.title: Mating types of Fusarium fujikuroi from bakanae disease of rice in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. M.; Bashar, M. A.; Sultana, R.
research_papers.key_findings: Identified both MAT-1 and MAT-2 mating types among Bangladeshi bakanae isolates; demonstrated seed-treatment with carbendazim or fludioxonil provides 90%+ control of seedling elongation.

research_papers.title: Advancing Salinity-Tolerant Rice in Bangladesh: The Case of BRRI dhan67 and Disease Dynamics
research_papers.authors: Kabir, M. S.; Salam, M. A.; Islam, M. R.
research_papers.key_findings: Assessed disease reaction of BRRI dhan67 across variable salinities; high ambient humidity in microclimates overrides salinity-induced leaf wax thickening to allow localized blast outbreaks.

research_papers.title: Assessing the Adoption and Adoption Gap of Selected BRRI Released Boro Rice Varieties in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Rahman, M. C.
research_papers.key_findings: Farmers report disease susceptibility (primarily neck blast and sheath blight) as the single primary reason for replacing older cultivars BRRI dhan28 and BRRI dhan29 with newer resistant varieties BRRI dhan89 and BRRI dhan92.

research_papers.title: Assessment of Genetic Diversity in Bangladeshi Rice Blast Pathogen Populations
research_papers.authors: Sultana, R.; Mia, M. A. T.; Latif, M. A.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Exploring Engineering
research_papers.key_findings: Field surveillance and engineering analysis: light trap catches of pest vectors and dew sensors predict spore release peaks in Boro seedbeds.

research_papers.title: Emergence of wheat blast in Bangladesh was caused by a South American lineage of Magnaporthe oryzae
research_papers.authors: Islam, M. T.; Croll, D.; Gladieux, P.; Soanes, D. M. et al.
research_papers.key_findings: Definitive peer-reviewed publication confirming emergence of South American MoT lineage in southwestern Bangladesh with 100% field yield loss on legacy cultivars.

research_papers.title: Wheat Blast: A New Fungal Inhabitant to Bangladesh Threatening World Wheat Production
research_papers.authors: Malaker, P. K.; Barma, N. C. D.; Tiwari, T. P.; Collis, W. J. et al.
research_papers.key_findings: Comprehensive epidemiological review: over 15,000 hectares affected in 2016 with yield losses up to 100%; documents symptom progression from bleached spikes to shriveled grain.

research_papers.title: Economic benefits of blast-resistant biofortified wheat in Bangladesh: The case of BARI Gom 33
research_papers.authors: Mottaleb, K. A.; Singh, P. K.; Sonderman, C. A.; Kruseman, G.
research_papers.key_findings: Adoption of 2NS-translocation carrying blast-resistant biofortified variety BARI Gom 33 delivers substantial national economic return, mitigating annual risk of $13 million in crop failure.

research_papers.title: Wheat blast disease: Bangladesh and global perspectives of blast resistance
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Kabir, M. S.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
research_papers.key_findings: Identified high vulnerability in legacy cultivars (Prodip, BARI Gom 26); confirmed resistance in BARI Gom 33 and WMRI breeding lines carrying the Aegilops ventricosa 2NS translocation segment.

research_papers.title: Effects of plant extracts on controlling wheat blast disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum pathotype in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Mahbub, M. S.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
research_papers.key_findings: Evaluated botanicals against MoT conidia; allicin-rich garlic extract and ginger rhizome extracts inhibited spore germination by 78% in in-vitro and spikelet assays.

research_papers.title: Oligomycins inhibit Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum and suppress wheat blast in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Chakraborty, M.; Mahmud, N. U.; Gupta, D. R.; Islam, M. T.
research_papers.geographic_scope: Bangladesh (Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Agricultural University, Gazipur)
research_papers.key_findings: Discovered that natural oligomycins from marine Streptomyces completely halt conidial germination and appressorium differentiation of Bangladeshi MoT isolates.

research_papers.title: Host Resistance to Spot Blotch (Bipolaris Sorokiniana) in Wheat across South Asia and Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Duveiller, E.; Sharma, R. C.; Joshi, A. K.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Management of Wheat and Barley Diseases
research_papers.key_findings: Documents Bipolaris sorokiniana spot blotch as the primary biotic constraint to wheat in the warm, humid plains of Bangladesh; yield reductions average 18-35% in susceptible genotypes.

research_papers.title: Effect of wheat cultivar mixtures on spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana) severity and yield in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Malaker, P. K.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
research_papers.key_findings: Pioneering field experimentation demonstrating that cultivar mixtures of resistant and moderately susceptible lines reduced area under disease progress curve (AUDPC) by 28%.

research_papers.title: Phylogeographic population diversity of Bipolaris sorokiniana causing spot blotch of wheat in South Asia
research_papers.authors: Aggarwal, R.; Gurjar, M. S.; Bashyal, B. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Genomic profiling shows high gene flow across Bangladesh and Eastern India wheat regions; pathotype 1-2 predominantly virulent on traditional varieties.

research_papers.title: Mitigating the twin problems of malnutrition and wheat blast by one wheat variety in Bangladesh: The Case of BARI Gom 33
research_papers.authors: Mottaleb, K. A.; Govindan, V.; Singh, P. K.; Sonder, K.
research_papers.key_findings: Detailed agronomic and biofortification study: BARI Gom 33 confers complete blast resistance via 2NS translocation while providing 51 mg/kg grain zinc.

research_papers.title: Variability of Bipolaris maydis in relation to maydis blight severity in maize
research_papers.authors: Singh, V.; Sharma, S.; Kumar, P.; Hooda, K. S.
research_papers.key_findings: Analyzed thermal and moisture response of 32 Bipolaris maydis isolates; optimum radial mycelial growth occurs at 28-30°C and 90% RH; conidial germination drops below 18°C.

research_papers.title: Management of Maydis Leaf Blight Disease of Maize Caused by Bipolaris maydis Using Biocontrol Agents and Fungicides
research_papers.authors: Devi, S.; Lal, A. A.; Simon, S.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
research_papers.key_findings: Foliar application of Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC at 1 mL/L demonstrated 74.8% disease reduction and 26.5% yield increase over untreated check.

research_papers.title: Morphological and Molecular Variation of Isolates Causing Maydis Leaf Blight in Subtropical Maize
research_papers.authors: Yadav, O. P.; Hossain, F.; Karjagi, C. G.
research_papers.key_findings: Characterized teleomorph Cochliobolus heterostrophus; Race T susceptibility confirmed in male sterile cytoplasm lines; Race O predominant across northern plains.

research_papers.disease: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii)
research_papers.title: Influence of Weather Parameters on Development of Maydis Leaf Blight in Maize
research_papers.authors: Kumar, A.; Singh, V.; Hooda, K. S.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
research_papers.key_findings: Correlated Maydis leaf blight progress with relative humidity >85% and maximum temperatures between 28-32°C; disease severity increased by 14% per day during persistent cloudiness.

research_papers.disease: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii)
research_papers.title: Rhizosphere Trichoderma isolates as potential biocontrol agent for Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight of Maize
research_papers.authors: Gautam, A.; Sharma, S.; Kumar, R.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy
research_papers.key_findings: Trichoderma asperellum effectively parasitized R. solani sclerotia in maize field soils, reducing seedling damping-off and basal sheath blight incidence by 58%.

research_papers.title: QTLs Mapping for Turcicum Leaf Blight Resistance in Maize (Zea Mays L.)
research_papers.authors: Rahman, M. M.; Ali, M. L.; Islam, M. R.
research_papers.key_findings: Identified major genomic QTLs on chromosome 2 and 5 imparting field tolerance against Exserohilum turcicum in BARI hybrid maize lines.

research_papers.title: Assessment of genetics for turcicum leaf blight resistance in maize (Zea mays L.) in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Rahman, M. M.; Islam, M. S.; Amiruzzaman, M.
research_papers.key_findings: Demonstrated additive gene action governing Ht1/Ht2 resistance genes against northern corn leaf blight; recommends winter sowing timing to escape humid sporulation peaks.

research_papers.title: Variability and traits association in maize (Zea mays L.) for yield and foliar health in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Amiruzzaman, M.; Islam, M. A.; Hassan, L.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
research_papers.key_findings: Evaluated 24 BARI hybrid maize genotypes; BARI Hybrid Maize-9 and BARI Hybrid Maize-7 exhibited minimal foliar blight progression and superior harvest index under Barind conditions.

research_papers.title: Efficacy of selected fungicides and antibacterial chemicals against Fusarium stalk rot in maize
research_papers.authors: Sharma, P.; Kumar, A.; Hooda, K. S.
research_papers.key_findings: Post-flowering water stress and lodging predispose stalks to vascular occlusion by Fusarium verticillioides; balanced potassium and soil drench with carbendazim suppress vascular breakdown.

research_papers.title: Responses of TIBA on growth, yield and disease tolerance components of BARI Maize in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Sultana, N.; Rahman, M. M.; Hossain, M. A.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Journal of Bangladesh Academy of Sciences
research_papers.key_findings: Canopy architecture modification via anti-auxin treatments enhanced lower canopy air circulation, significantly reducing microclimatic humidity and sheath blight progression.

research_papers.title: Ralstonia solanacearum: A Threat to Potato Production in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Miah, M. N. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Hossain, M. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Landmark Bangladesh study replacing erroneous prior citation: documents Ralstonia solanacearum race 3 biovar 2 as dominant pathogen causing up to 45% vascular tuber rot in northern Bangladesh; proves disease occurs primarily when warm soil temperatures (>28°C) coincide with excess soil moisture/waterlogging, with zero foliar leaf wetness requirement.

research_papers.title: Profitability and Disease Reaction of BARI Released Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) Varieties in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Sarker, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Evaluated Diamant, Cardinal, BARI Alu-7, and BARI Alu-8; documented late blight and bacterial wilt loss differentials; verified benefit-cost ratio of 1.82 with timely preventative fungicidal sprays.

research_papers.title: Canopy Reflectance Measurements Used to Estimate Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) Severity in Potato
research_papers.authors: Popescu, S.; Donescu, V.; Ilie, M.
research_papers.key_findings: Demonstrates that multispectral vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, and red edge position) reliably capture foliar late blight destruction 4-6 days before visible chlorosis expands.

research_papers.title: Impact of potato var. BARI Alu-25 adoption on the growers’ livelihood and disease incidence in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Rashid, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Adoption of moderately late-blight resistant cultivar BARI Alu-25 reduced necessary fungicide applications from 7-9 sprays per season to 2-3 sprays, raising farmer net income by 34%.

research_papers.title: Adoption and profitability of BARI released potato varieties in northern region of Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.; Rashid, M. A.
research_papers.key_findings: Evaluated Diamant, Cardinal, BARI Alu-7, and BARI Alu-25 across 300 commercial farms; shows that disease-free certified foundation seed tubers eliminate 80% of primary bacterial wilt and PLRV infections.

research_papers.title: Screening of Exotic and Local Potato Germplasm against Potato Virus PVX, PVY and PLRV
research_papers.authors: Khan, M. A.; Rashid, A.; Ahmad, I.
research_papers.key_findings: Myzus persicae aphid vectors transmit Potato Leaf Roll Virus (PLRV) and PVY during mid-season warming (January-February); roguing infected seed potatoes within 4 weeks after emergence prevents field degeneration.

research_papers.title: Tomato leaf curl Patna virus causing tomato leaf curl disease in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Roy, B.; Islam, M. S.; Akhter, S.; Malaker, P. K.
research_papers.key_findings: Confirmed molecular identity of Begomovirus causing up to 85% yield reduction in commercial tomato fields in Bangladesh; identified transmission exclusively through sweetpotato whitefly Bemisia tabaci.

research_papers.title: Association of tomato leaf curl Gujarat virus and tomato leaf curl Bangladesh virus with tomato leaf curl disease in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Sultana, R.; Islam, M. T.; Brown, J. K.
research_papers.key_findings: Revealed mixed begomovirus infections and betasatellite complexes driving aggressive curling, stunting, and flower abortion; validates vector control with yellow sticky traps and systemic neonicotinoid seedlings drenches.

research_papers.disease: Bacterial Wilt & Soil-Borne Disease in Tomato
research_papers.title: Combination of biological control agents and garlic (Allium sativum) extract against bacterial and fungal wilt of tomato in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Islam, M. R.; Akter, N.; Hossain, M. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Combined soil application of Trichoderma harzianum and aqueous garlic clove extract (1:10) suppressed bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) and Fusarium oxysporum incidence by 62% in summer tomato plots.

research_papers.title: Tomato Cultivation in Bangladesh: Insights into Pest Awareness and Disease Management
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. S.; Mian, M. A. H.; Rahman, M. M.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Agriculture and Biology
research_papers.key_findings: Surveys farm-level disease occurrence: Early blight (Alternaria solani) and Late blight (P. infestans) are primary foliar bottlenecks in winter tomatoes; Difenoconazole (0.05%) and Mancozeb (0.2%) remain standard DAE treatments.

research_papers.title: Bio-rational management for root-knot and wilt disease complex of tomato in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Rahman, M. A.; Ahmad, M. U.; Hossain, I.
research_papers.key_findings: Meloidogyne incognita wounding exacerbates Ralstonia solanacearum ingress; mustard oilcake (300 kg/ha) and Paecilomyces lilacinus soil amendment suppressed root galling and vascular wilt simultaneously.

research_papers.title: Progressive impact of alternaria blight on antioxidants enzyme of mustard (Brassica campestris L.) in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Sarker, B. C.; Roy, B.; Hasan, M. M.
research_papers.key_findings: Shows Alternaria brassicae infection severely reduces catalase and superoxide dismutase activity, leading to premature pod shattering and 32-55% seed yield deficit in Tori-7 and BARI Sarisha-14 under heavy dew conditions.

research_papers.title: Studies on management of Alternaria blight (Alternaria brassicae) of mustard through fungicides and bio-agents
research_papers.authors: Choudhary, R.; Singh, S. K.; Kumar, A.
research_papers.key_findings: Foliar spray of Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L) at 45 and 60 days after sowing achieved 76.4% disease control and maximized 1000-seed weight and oil content.

research_papers.title: Harnessing Hypovirulence: Mycovirus-induced modulation of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum on Brassica crops
research_papers.authors: Sharma, P.; Kumar, V.; Rai, P. K.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Agricultural and Plant Science
research_papers.key_findings: Sclerotinia stem rot emerges in high-fertility winter mustard when canopy closes; sclerotia carpogenically germinate under moist soil and temperatures 15-20°C, releasing airborne ascospores infecting senescent petals.

research_papers.title: Efficacy of fungicides to control Stemphylium blight (Stemphylium botryosum) in lentil in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. S.; Bakr, M. A.; Dey, T. K.
research_papers.key_findings: Pioneering BARI research establishing Rovral 50 WP (Iprodione @ 2 g/L) and Secure 600 WG (Fenamidone + Mancozeb @ 1.5 g/L) as most effective fungicides, reducing Stemphylium leaf blighting by 71% and lifting seed yield by 45%.

research_papers.title: Epidemiology of Stemphylium Blight of Lentil in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Bakr, M. A.; Ahmed, H. U.; Rahman, M. M.
research_papers.journal_or_publisher: Bangladesh Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research
research_papers.key_findings: Quantified weather triggers: night temperature 18-22°C, relative humidity >85%, and dense canopy morning dew duration >6 hours promote explosive conidiophore proliferation in February.

research_papers.title: Race identification in Uromyces vicia-fabae causing lentil rust and host response
research_papers.authors: Kumar, S.; Saxena, D. R.; Basandrai, A. K.
research_papers.key_findings: Delineated virulent pathotypes across sub-Himalayan lentil tracts; verified high resistance in BARI Masur-6 and BARI Masur-8 against prevalent teliospore populations.

research_papers.title: Chili anthracnose: Colletotrichum species complex, biology, and management
research_papers.authors: Saxena, A.; Raghuwanshi, R.; Gupta, V. K.; Singh, H. B.
research_papers.geographic_scope: South Asia / Tropical chili growing regions
research_papers.key_findings: Documents Colletotrichum capsici and C. gloeosporioides as primary causal agents of fruit rot and dieback; splash dispersal occurs during warm rainy intervals (27-30°C, RH >80%); recommended spray program with azoxystrobin and copper oxychloride.

research_papers.title: Forecasting Anthracnose (Colletotrichum capsici) Attack on Chili Using Microclimate Correlation
research_papers.authors: Widiastuti, A.; Suryanti, S.; Ningrum, P.
research_papers.key_findings: Mathematical correlation models confirm fruit rot incidence spikes when rain events coincide with temperatures >26°C and surface fruit wetness >5 hours.

research_papers.title: Eco-friendly Management of Purple Blotch (Alternaria Porri (Ellis) Cif.) of Onion (Allium Cepa L.) in Bangladesh
research_papers.authors: Hossain, M. I.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
research_papers.key_findings: Direct Bangladesh field trial: Trichoderma harzianum bio-agent and garlic bulb extract combined with Mancozeb (Dithane M-45 @ 0.2%) provided 73.5% reduction in purple blotch leaf lesions and boosted bulb yield by 31.8%.
